lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.23 - A Listen and write T (True) or F (False).

details: Listen and write T (True) or F (False) checks students' recall of the target vocabulary from Units 1 and 2 (clothes, accessories, attractions and feelings), and gives them the opportunity to practise listening for detail.
Look for careful listening, accurate identification of the target vocabulary, and correct labelling of the boxes with T or F.

“What do you like to do for fun? I like shopping! And I really like amusement parks. They are exciting! But I’m not sure what’s happening in the pictures. Are they having fun? Let’s listen and choose!”

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together: 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

details: Listen and choose reviews the target language and key structures from Units 1 and 2 and offers a further opportunity to practise listening for detail.
Look for careful listening, accurate identification of the pictures based on the descriptions, and correct circling of the letters.
“Great listening! I want to find out more about the things the children saw at the shops and how they felt at the amusement park. Can you help me to listen and choose the correct answers?”

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.23 - C. Listen and write.

details: Listen and write gives students another opportunity to practise their listening skills, think about appropriate answers to the questions based on the pictures, and practise using the key structures and target language to form complete sentences.

Look for careful listening, accurate identification of the pictures, correct word choice and word order, appropriate tense, correct spelling, a full stop at the end of the sentences, and neat writing on the lines.
“Great job! Hmmm… I’m really not sure what these children are doing - or how they felt. Does that look like a scary film? Let’s listen and try to find out!”

details: Look and write gives students controlled practice identifying and spelling target language from the units. It also reinforces neat handwriting.

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.24 - D. Listen and read.

details: Listen and read allows students to review the key structures and target language from Units 1 and 2, learn some new words, and practise their literacy skills.
Look for careful listening, students following the text while they listen, and clear pronunciation, steady pacing, and correct identification of each word while they read.
“Look, a big rollercoaster. That looks scary! Where do you think that photo was taken? Shall we listen and read and find out?”

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.24 - E. Choose or write the correct answers. 10m]

details: Choose or write the correct answers checks students’ understanding of the text and gives them an opportunity to practise reading for understanding.
Look for correct circling/writing of the answers and the ability to identify where in the text they found the answers.
“Amazing World sounds… well… amazing! I can’t remember everything the writer said about it though. What did they do first? Was there a gift shop? I am sure you know the answer!”

Heads Up (Reading): 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and help Ss to understand the text by asking questions, practicing skimming (reading for gist), scanning (reading for specific information) and detail (reading for comprehension). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down (Listen and Chant): 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together (Video Chant): 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4R
